To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microservices research needs a community-owned architecture that is: (i) based on an existing architecture that can be extended, (ii) based on a set of well-defined requirements that are representative of the real-world applications, and (iii) based on a well-defined evaluation methodology.

the following requirements for microservices benchmarks are important to consider: (i) microservices benchmarks should be based on real-world microservices applications, (ii) they should be open source, (iii) they should be based on the latest microservices technology, (iv) the source code and documentation should be available, (v) they should be easy to use, (vi) they should be scalable and (vii) they should have a well-defined and documented evaluation methodology

the following requirements are necessary to support repeatable research on the development of microservices architecture: (a) a benchmark should be based on an architecture that can be implemented in multiple languages; (b) the architecture should be sufficiently flexible to enable the implementation of a variety of applications; (c) the benchmark should be based upon a realistic application that is representative of the types of applications that are currently being developed in industry; (d) the architecture should include an appropriate set of microservices and their interactions
